correctness.rationale: For the stated exactly mass-preserving predictor and mean-value gradients, Gram elimination gives G_p(mu+z)=mu+w+(ρ²−r²)(w+z)/||w+z||², with determinant ||w+z||²/4. The initialized orbit is radial with t_{j+1}=(rt_j+ρ²)/(r+t_j), positive t_j, and Cayley coordinate (t_j−ρ)/(t_j+ρ)=κ^{j+1}. A nonsingular fixed point is feasible by the discrete chain rule. For r>0, z−w is parallel to z+w with proportionality not equal to one, so z=±ρw/r; the negative root is excluded exactly at r=ρ, and Cauchy–Schwarz gives the nearest positive root. At r=0 the initialization has rank one but the entire target sphere consists of nonsingular fixed points. For r<ρ, a=−κ, even j passes iff a^{j+1}≤ε/(2−ε) and odd j needs the smaller threshold ε/(2+ε). An even candidate attains the lower bound for any successful j up to two updates, and −log a=2r/ρ+O((r/ρ)^3), proving the sharp coefficient. The first iterate is (r²+ρ²)/(2r). On u⊥, J²=−I, so the explicit RK predictor polynomial is (1−h²)(I+hJ); r/ρ=2√2|h−1|+O((h−1)²), giving the singular start and coefficient 1/(4√2) times the stated logarithm. The frozen count uses distance to the selected limit, not the residual tolerance of Pu–Ran Algorithm 1. value.rationale: The theorem diagnoses a genuine numerical limitation not visible from existence of a nearby feasible corrected solution: the selected endpoint stays bounded while the actual initialized solver makes an arbitrarily large excursion and takes order ρ/r iterations at fixed accuracy. An explicit, valid conservative ODE predictor can reach the singular state at a finite step. This makes the branch and work distinction useful for implementing or safeguarding such corrections; the example does not purport to show accurate integration at that large step.
